title: Shuntline
status: core + cabinet in PR; iterations in PR; dossier is iteration 10
summary: The shunting yard behind the Prismheart arcade row, where the night goods train is made up for the valley halts. Carriages tagged for destinations arrive in a seeded order on the inbound track; the yardmaster sends each one straight out, parks it on a short siding, or pulls a parked carriage back out, and the outbound train must leave with its tags never going down. A move budget keeps the shift honest. Every train is solvable by construction; the craft is which carriages to park, on which siding, in which order. Deterministic per seed, bit-exact between the Python rules, the C++ core and the Unreal cabinet.

mechanics.name: Train
mechanics.text: 7 / 9 / 11 carriages tagged 1..3 / 1..4 / 1..5 drawn in order. Setup redraws the train (up to 50 times) until the exact search sorts it within the move budget, so every shift can be finished.

mechanics.name: Moves
mechanics.text: out sends the front carriage to the outbound track; s<n> shunts it onto siding n (2 / 2 / 3 sidings, each a stack of at most 3); p<n> pulls siding n's top carriage out. Every move costs one of 16 / 20 / 24.

mechanics.name: Order
mechanics.text: The outbound tags may never go down: a carriage tagged below the last one out can never leave, whether on the inbound track or under a higher tag on a siding. Such moves are refused, not punished.

mechanics.name: End of shift
mechanics.text: Every carriage out makes up the train: 10 per destination present on the outbound track plus 2 per move left. The moves running out, or no legal move left (the yard is blocked), ends the shift with 10 per destination already out.

mechanics.name: Yardmaster (demo)
mechanics.text: An exact search over (inbound index, sidings, last tag out, moves left): actions in the rules' order, states pruned when more carriages remain than moves, when any carriage is tagged below the last out, or when a siding holds a lower tag under a higher one; memoised; 20,000-node budget (under 700 in practice). It makes up every seeded train; send-out-when-you-can play wins about 2 / 0 / 0 percent.

mechanics.name: Preview
mechanics.text: preview(move) gives the carriage moved and whether it leaves the yard, without moving it; the native sweep proves it equals the real move.

mechanics.name: Guide (option 1)
mechanics.text: Practice mode marks the yardmaster's move in blue (the front carriage for out, the siding for a shunt or pull) and the hint names it. In both modes carriages that can never leave carry a red bar, and the hint says so when the front carriage is one of them.

mechanics.name: Saves
mechanics.text: Text save (shared DaedalusDesktopSaveText shape): difficulty, seed, the move list of the shift, the picked siding, score, over, won. Restore replays the moves on the seeded train and refuses a save whose score or flags the replay does not reach; Python from_state checks counts, order, lengths and the end flags directly.

mechanics.name: Controls
mechanics.text: Up/Down (or stick) pick a siding; Right sends the front carriage out; A / J / Space shunt it onto the picked siding; K / pad B pull that siding's top carriage out; R or pad Start restart a finished shift. Cabinet class DesktopGames/DaedalusDesktopShuntlineCore.h, registry id shuntline, save slot shuntline.dgs.

items.text: A short four-wheel van with its destination tag painted on the side; amber on the board, teal once on the outbound track, red-barred when it can never leave.
The arrival road, front carriage nearest the switch.
A stub road with a stop block holding up to three carriages, last in first out.
The departure road where the train is made up in tag order.
The MOVES counter; the cue turns to 'Moves are tight' when the carriages left nearly equal the moves left.

storyline.text: The night goods for the valley halts has to leave in station order, and the arrival road has it all jumbled; the yardmaster hands you the lamp.
Three rows on the first move: out sends the front carriage, s<n> parks it and p<n> pulls it back, and the outbound tags never go down. (They leave after the first move.)
Each difficulty is a longer train with more destinations: 7 carriages for 3 halts with 2 sidings, 9 for 4, then 11 for 5 with a third siding and only a little slack in the moves.
The last carriage couples on in order and the train is made up; every move left on the clock is the stationmaster's thanks.
The shift clock runs out, or the yard blocks with a low tag buried under a high one. Pad A or R brings the same train in again so the parking can be planned.
The shunting yard sits at the far end of the Prismheart arcade row after the wall yard; a side craft, not a campaign gate, and made-up trains add to the arcade scoreboard.
